children: Renewed fighting in the Persian Gulf pushed U.S. oil prices back above $90 a barrel, adding inflationary pressure to the bond rout that has lifted yields on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes to the highest level of President Trump's term.

Front-month U.S. oil futures settled today at $90.22 a barrel, up 5.2% on the day and 8.2% over the past two trading sessions. The benchmark crude price had dropped below $70 in July before a U.S-Iran ceasefire fizzled.

Most crucially from an inflationary perspective, diesel futures rose more than 6% today in New York to end at $4.6773 a gallon, the third highest closing price ever. They have gained more than 10% over the past five trading days. National average retail prices for the trucking, farming and construction fuel hit $5.63 a gallon, nearly $2 higher than a year ago, according to Dow Jones Energy.
